items.title: Jordan Prayer Times
items.shortDescription: Official prayer times for Jordan on phone, Wear OS and Android TV, with alarms that keep scheduling themselves, plus Ramadan and Friday reminders, Adhkar, Qibla and Quran.
items.description:
Jordan Prayer Times delivers the official Ministry of Awqaf prayer times for every region of Jordan, built around one goal: alarms that actually fire. They are scheduled through Android's alarm clock system, so they survive Doze and battery saver, show the alarm icon in the status bar, and take over the lock screen with the Athan.

Version 3.0 makes that self-sustaining: the moment the last prayer of the day rings, tomorrow is scheduled — and a check every couple of hours, another shortly before each prayer, and a background sync keep it that way without the app ever being opened. It also keeps a record of every alarm that fired and how late it was, so a missed one can be explained instead of argued about.

New in 3.0: Ramadan suhoor and iftar reminders that appear only during Ramadan, worked out on the device from the Hijri date; a Jumu'ah reminder on Fridays; any audio file on the phone as an Athan; an optional sunrise alarm; snooze; and home screen widgets you can restyle — theme, transparency, text colours, even their own language, separate from the app.

Version 2.6 brought the Adhkar section with 287 adhkar from Hisnul Muslim and a tap-to-count tasbih, wudu and adhkar reminders tied to prayer times, two resizable widgets, per-prayer alarm switches, 12/24-hour and Hijri date settings, and layouts that fit phones and tablets.

Alongside that: an interactive Qibla compass and GPS map, the complete Quran with audio, translations, Tafsir and bookmarks, a full Arabic and English interface with RTL and the Hijri calendar, and a Wear OS companion with a tile and a watch face complication, built with Hazem Afaneh.

The Android TV edition, built with Ehab Amawi in native Kotlin, puts the official times on the big screen: today's prayers, a prayer calendar with Hijri dates, and a screensaver that shows the time and the next prayer over credited photos of Jordan's mosques and landmarks, in Arabic or English.

Everything works offline after first setup, with no accounts, no ads and no tracking.
items.stack: Flutter | Kotlin | Node JS
items.platform: Android | Wear OS | Android TV | iOS
highlights: Alarms that survive Doze and battery saver and reschedule themselves
One product on phone, Wear OS and Android TV
Fully offline — no accounts, no ads, no tracking

items.title: Escrow Payments Service & ERP Integration
items.shortDescription: A provider-agnostic escrow payment broker, and the ERP flow built on it
items.description:
A provider-agnostic escrow payments microservice built in Laravel that brokers a licensed escrow provider behind one stable internal API, so internal systems integrate with three values — base URL, client id and secret — and never learn the provider behind it. Every money-moving write is idempotent on the caller's own reference, so a retry through a provider outage cannot pay a seller twice. Two-directional webhooks: provider notification batches ingested idempotently, and per-client callbacks delivered from a queue with retries and full delivery logs. It ships multi-environment (separate sandbox and production provider paths with per-environment credentials), with an admin console for client onboarding and credential rotation, health probes, and scheduled safety-net jobs that fill in a confirmation that never arrived.

The second half is the ERP integration: a parallel payment path added to a live ERPNext deployment without altering the flow carrying current volume — seller registration and virtual IBAN issuance, a three-step clearing process, ledger postings driven only by confirmed provider callbacks, refunds, reconciliation actions for a lost callback, and SLA monitoring with operational reporting.
items.stack: Laravel | PHP 8.4 | MySQL | MongoDB | Redis | Docker | Frappe/ERPNext | Python
highlights: Idempotent money movement — a retry can never pay a seller twice
Two-way webhooks with queued retries and full delivery logs
New payment path added to a live ERPNext without touching current volume

items.title: Telegram Multi-Bot AI Platform (v2)
items.shortDescription: A self-hosted platform that runs many Telegram bots from one React dashboard: API bots, Stable Diffusion image bots and LLM chatbots, all on local AI.
items.description:
My own take on a multi-bot platform, built for a different purpose from the client system I delivered for Maple: where that one turns bot commands into API calls, this one is mainly a local AI platform. One deployment runs three kinds of Telegram bot, side by side, each in its own OS process so one crash never takes the others down.

API bots turn slash-commands into HTTP calls, with a command builder that imports cURL, runs test requests, picks response fields and keeps a history. Image bots generate and inpaint with Stable Diffusion through a shared Redis job queue, with masks drawn by hand or detected automatically by YOLOv8, Segment Anything, YOLO-World or CLIPSeg from a text description. Chatbots run on Ollama locally or OpenRouter, with personas, long-term memory kept as a rolling summary, image understanding through a vision model, and generated pictures that keep a character's look consistent. A prompt helper writes Stable Diffusion prompts with a local LLM and translates Arabic to English offline, so nothing leaves the machine.

The same codebase runs on an NVIDIA GPU, a CPU or an Intel iGPU through OpenVINO; the launcher detects the hardware and picks the stack. The React and TypeScript dashboard is live over Redis Pub/Sub and server-sent events: stat cards, notifications, a queue monitor with progress and cancel, a GPU, CPU and memory monitor, and a console of every container's logs through a scoped Docker socket proxy. Roles with a per-target permission matrix, Argon2id passwords, a generation gallery and nightly Postgres backups round it out. The screenshot shows a demo install with made-up bots.
items.stack: Python | FastAPI | python-telegram-bot | PostgreSQL | Redis | Stable Diffusion | Ollama | YOLOv8 | SAM | React | TypeScript | Tailwind | Docker
items.platform: Web dashboard | Telegram | Docker (NVIDIA, CPU, Intel iGPU)
highlights: API, image-generation and LLM chatbots from one dashboard
Runs on NVIDIA, CPU or Intel iGPU from the same codebase
Automatic inpainting masks with YOLOv8, SAM and CLIPSeg

items.title: Kids Mode
items.shortDescription: Hand your phone to your child safely: only the apps you choose, with the notification bar, settings and power menu locked away. No root needed.
items.description:
Kids Mode lets a parent hand their phone to a child safely: the child sees a friendly Kids screen with only the apps the parent chose, and nothing else is in reach. It brings back the Kids Mode that Transsion (TECNO / Infinix / itel) phones shipped with before an update removed it, and it works on any Android phone.

The full lock needs no root, no computer and no Shizuku: Kids Mode pairs once with the phone's own Wireless debugging and runs its own on-device ADB client, then switches off the notification bar, quick settings, recent apps and the power-button shortcuts at system level, and grants itself everything else it needs. An accessibility guard sends the child straight back to the Kids screen from any app, Settings, assistant or link they weren't allowed, and device admin stops it from being uninstalled. After a reboot the phone goes straight back to Kids Mode.

Parents get time limits and forced breaks that close the open app and show a break timer, a maximum volume, per-app usage for today and the last 7 days, and PIN, fingerprint or face unlock. Eye comfort adds a warm screen filter and a too-close warning that uses the proximity sensor or, on phones where it can't be used, the front camera with on-device ML Kit face detection, calibrated to each phone and nothing saved.

Phone calls still come through, a calm night-sky theme is gentler on young eyes, and every screen is in English and Arabic with a full right-to-left layout. No account, no ads, no tracking: nothing leaves the phone.
items.stack: Kotlin | Jetpack Compose | ML Kit | On-device ADB | Accessibility Service
highlights: Full system lock with no root: pairs with the phone's own Wireless debugging
Time limits, forced breaks and a max-volume cap, all unlocked by PIN or biometrics
Too-close eye warning with on-device ML Kit, nothing saved or sent

items.title: KB Portal: My Mind as an Interactive AI
items.shortDescription: A self-hosted AI that answers as me, only from my own knowledge base, with a citation on every claim. Local-first, bilingual, and honest when it doesn't know.
items.description:
KB Portal turns what I know about myself (my CV, my portfolio, my projects and my notes) into an AI you can talk to. Ask it anything and it answers in my voice, only from that knowledge base, with a citation on every claim; if the answer isn't in there, it says so instead of guessing.

The retrieval is built to never miss anything. When the whole knowledge base fits in the model's context window, which it reads from each model's metadata, all of it goes into the prompt; when it doesn't, a hybrid search in Qdrant merges dense bge-m3 embeddings with BM25 using Reciprocal Rank Fusion, packs whole chunks up to the budget and refuses weak matches. After each answer a self-audit pass asks the model what the context holds that it left out, and appends it, which in testing caught projects the models were still skipping. Chunks are ordered the same way every time so the prompt prefix stays identical and the model's cache is reused; a warmup after every sync means the heavy prefill happens once, not on every question.

Ingestion reads markdown by heading, PDFs by page, JSON, HTML and even git repositories, and a sync every six hours skips unchanged sources by hash. It runs locally on Ollama by default, with optional cloud models and a thinking-effort dial, answers in the language of the question, and flips the whole interface to Arabic right to left. Everything binds to localhost by default, with an optional password, rate limiting and server-side stripping so no file paths or raw text ever reach the browser. The screenshot shows answers drawn from my public CV and portfolio.
items.stack: Python | FastAPI | Qdrant | Ollama | bge-m3 | BM25 | JavaScript | Tailwind | Docker
highlights: Answers only from my knowledge base, with a citation on every claim
Hybrid dense + BM25 retrieval, or the whole knowledge base when it fits
Self-audit pass catches what the first answer left out

items.title: Quote Factory
items.shortDescription: A self-hosted pipeline that turns Arabic and English quotes into YouTube Shorts, never repeating a quote, style, clip or track, and publishes them on a schedule.
items.description:
Quote Factory is a self-hosted pipeline that turns bilingual Arabic and English quotes into YouTube Shorts and publishes them on a schedule, all from one web dashboard. One press of Generate new runs the whole chain: fetch a quote (alternating between authentic Arabic and English sources, so half the channel isn't translated), translate it, pick a background clip and a music track nobody has used, render, and write the title, description and hashtags. Then it stops and waits: nothing uploads without a review and an approval.

Every video is typed out letter by letter at one steady rhythm, with both languages advancing together so neither audience waits for the other, the author on a single line between them, and which language sits on top rotating by video. Arabic is re-shaped at every step so the letters join correctly mid-word. Each render samples a point in a design space of 2.7 trillion styles (fonts, colour, layout, camera motion, grain and more), hashes it and refuses any style already used, and the same zero-repeat rule, enforced in the database, covers quotes, background clips and music. Downloaded tracks and beds composed on the spot alternate one for one, the composed ones built from seven instrument archetypes and hashed into a signature, so no two videos share a sound and every track's licence is recorded before it is ever published.

Approved videos get publish slots at least four hours apart and go out through the YouTube Data API. A check every five minutes catches up on missed slots even after the machine was switched off. Views, retention and likes come back through the Analytics API, and an insights page compares performance by length, language, theme and music to answer what to make more of. A Telegram bot mirrors the dashboard: notifications, a daily summary, approvals and corrections to a translation from the chat, with buttons that stay under the text box and a queue that advances to the next video by itself.

It runs as three Docker containers (Postgres, a Flask dashboard behind gunicorn, and a job worker on a Postgres queue), and every outside service it uses has a free tier.
items.stack: Python | Flask | PostgreSQL | FFmpeg | Docker | YouTube Data API | Telegram Bot API | htmx | Tailwind
highlights: One button: quote, translation, clip, music, render and metadata
Zero repetition of quotes, styles, clips and music, enforced in the database
Scheduled publishing, analytics insights and Telegram control

items.title: Jservices — A Personal Google Workspace
items.shortDescription: A self-hosted suite that recreates Gmail, Photos, Drive, Messages and voice recordings behind one launcher, with search across everything and an admin back office.
items.description:
A personal, self-hosted take on Google Workspace: one launcher opens mail, photos, drive, messages and voice recordings, all sharing a single contacts graph, with one search that spans every module at once.

Mail has threaded conversations, starring, folders and contacts; Drive has nested folders and per-file pages; Photos tags people and flags images; Messages keeps conversations with direction and last-message tracking; and there's an audio recordings module. Behind it all is a full admin back office to manage every content type, a bulk import endpoint and file uploads.

Built with Next.js 16 (App Router) and React 19 in TypeScript, Prisma over SQLite, NextAuth with bcrypt for the admin, and Tailwind. The screenshot shows a demo instance with sample data.

highlights: Mail, photos, drive, messages and recordings in one suite

items.title: WhatsApp Exported Chat Viewer
items.shortDescription: Browse and analyse exported WhatsApp chats offline, in an interface that looks like WhatsApp Web, with search, a media gallery and statistics.
items.description:
A viewer for the chats WhatsApp lets you export, as a text file or a zip with media, shown in an interface styled after WhatsApp Web so they read the way they looked on the phone. It opens both Android and iOS export formats, and runs as a web app and as an Android app from one codebase.

Large chats with years of photos are the hard case, so the work went into speed: media is unzipped in a Web Worker so the interface never freezes, images appear one by one as they are extracted, and everything is cached in IndexedDB with versioning and a 30-day expiry, so opening the same chat again is instant. Up to three chats are preloaded in parallel with a progress bar, and the message list uses virtual scrolling, so only what is on screen is rendered, with jump-to-message from search.

A statistics view charts messages per hour, per day and per participant, with activity heatmaps and top contributors, next to gallery tabs for images, videos, audio and files. Search works across every chat or inside one, messages can be bookmarked, and the layout is built mobile first with a collapsible sidebar. The screenshot shows a made-up demo chat.
items.stack: React 19 | TypeScript | Vite | Jotai | IndexedDB | Web Workers | Capacitor
highlights: Media unzipped in a Web Worker, cached in IndexedDB
Virtual scrolling and cross-chat search for very large chats
Charts of activity by hour, day and participant

items.title: Credential Vault & API
items.shortDescription: A team credential manager: one place for the API keys, tokens and logins each environment uses, with per-environment roles, an audit log, a REST API and Swagger docs.
items.description:
A web app and REST API that keeps the credentials a team uses in each environment (dev, QA, pre-production, production) in one place instead of scattered across chats and configs, governed by per-environment permissions: each user gets view, create, update or delete rights per environment, with a superadmin role that can't be locked out.

items.title: Finance Tracker
items.shortDescription: A personal finance app for the web and Android that uses a Git repository as its database, so every change is a commit with full history.
items.description:
A household finance tracker for credit-card installments, loans, money owed and monthly expenses, with salaries feeding a monthly budget breakdown: what's due this month, what's left after debts, and what's left after expenses.

Instead of a server, it uses a Git repository as its database. Data is read and written through the GitHub Contents API, fetching the file's SHA before every write, so every change becomes a commit and the full history comes for free. It is deliberately online-only: if the repository can't be reached it stops with a clear error rather than show a stale copy. Changes are detected by comparing snapshots, so the sync button only appears when something changed, and a sync preview lists exactly what will be pushed.

Installments count down with progress bars and payments grouped by billing month. Deletes are instant with a five-second undo, cards toggle paid with a tap, and pull-to-refresh, dark and light themes and a custom modal system round out the interface. One plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript codebase ships as a web app and, through Capacitor, an Android app, and a build-time flag produces a read-only viewer build from the same code. The screenshot shows made-up data.
items.stack: JavaScript | HTML | CSS | Capacitor | GitHub Contents API
highlights: A Git repository as the database: every change is a commit
Sync preview and change detection before anything is pushed
One codebase for web and Android, with a read-only viewer build

items.title: Our Days
items.shortDescription: A small offline Android app that counts the family's birthdays and anniversaries, time since and time until, down to the second, with a live home-screen widget.
items.description:
Our Days keeps the dates that matter to a family in one calm place: for every birthday and anniversary it shows how long it has been and how long until the next one, ticking every second, with a year-progress ring around each person and the next date featured at the top. When two dates fall on the same day, the page splits into two columns.

The interesting part is the native home-screen widget. Android only refreshes widgets every 30 minutes, so the widget uses Chronometer views counting down on their own, an AlarmManager alarm at each change and one at midnight, which keeps it live to the second without draining the battery. It resizes to the height the launcher gives it, adds a row per person, and has its own settings screen: night or white card, background opacity, a colour for every element and a live preview, set separately for each widget.

The app is a Capacitor web view with vanilla JavaScript for the main screen and native Java for the widget and its settings, drawn edge to edge behind the system bars. Everything is bundled in the APK: no network, no accounts, no tracking.
items.stack: JavaScript | Capacitor | Java | Android Widgets | AlarmManager
highlights: Live countdowns to the second, for every date
Native widget that stays live beyond Android's 30-minute refresh
Per-widget colours, opacity and themes with a live preview

items.title: MBF Enhanced Git Terminal
items.shortDescription: A git-aware Bash prompt and a 20-command git CLI: staged, modified, stashed and ahead/behind at a glance, plus pull requests on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure from one command.
items.description:
About 3,400 lines of Bash that make the terminal tell you everything about a repository before you ask. A three-line prompt shows the time, the active Python environment and the user, then the branch and its remote with counts of staged, modified, untracked and stashed files and commits ahead or behind, all from a single git status pass, then the last exit code when a command failed.

It detects a rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in progress, shows the last commit's hash, message, age and author, tags and dirty submodules, warns about stale branches and runaway ahead/behind counts, and hides the detail automatically when the repository is clean. Four themes and a config file let every symbol and threshold be changed.

Next to it, mgit adds more than twenty git workflows: repository stats, branch cleanup, branch comparison with conflict detection, worktrees, a commit graph and timeline, search, undo and fixup, conflict helpers, and pull requests that detect whether the remote is GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps. An interactive installer backs up shell files before touching them, never adds its lines twice, and uninstalls cleanly.
items.stack: Bash | Git | GitHub CLI | GitLab CLI | Azure CLI
highlights: Staged, modified, stashed and ahead/behind in the prompt
Detects rebase, merge, cherry-pick and bisect in progress
mgit: 20+ workflows, PRs on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure
